newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Strangle bought in Reuters.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Strangle bought in Reuters.

text.p: An expectation of increased volatility in the shares of news and information company Reuters Holdings on Thursday prompted one trader to establish a long strangle traded options, dealers said.
The deal was to buy 1,000 April 650 puts at 15p and 1,000 April 700 calls at 28p.
At expiry, if the underlying shares are either below 607p or above 743p, the strangle will have some value and the buyer will make a profit.
A maximum loss of 43p will be made if the shares stay between 650p and 700p.
By 1525 GMT, Reuters' shares were up 18p to 702p.
Over in supermarket chain Asda Group the main deal was the purchase of 500 April 120 calls at 7-1/2p requiring the shares to go above 127-1/2p by expiry before a profit can be realised.

Elsewhere, in distilling and brewing group Guinness a near-term bear position was believed to have been rolled forward. This involved selling 400 February 460 puts at 19p in a closing deal and the purchase of 400 May 460 puts at 32p.
For a profit the new position requires the shares to go below 428p by expiry.
Meanwhile, in drinks company Allied Domecq, there was a buyer of 250 April 420 calls at 21p.
